u02-rem-early.resolution: I checked each flag against the Greek and found no meaning error. οὐ γὰρ ἐν μνήμῃ γε, φησίν, ὢν παρὰ σοὶ σκυθρωπὸς ἂν διῆγον καὶ … ἐθλιβόμην: the participle ὤν is the protasis ('if I were in remembrance with you'). οὐ, not μή, shows that the negative belongs to the apodosis with ἄν ('I would not be going about in gloom'). Read as 'not being in remembrance, I would go about gloomy', the sentence would invert the psalmist's complaint (Why have you forgotten me? Why do I go mourning?). 'Psalm 12:2 (13:1)', 'Psalm 29:10 (30:9)' and 'Psalm 17:2 (18:1)' are correct LXX/English pairs. 'Why then is what is yours not accomplished, but what comes from us abounds?' renders Ἵνα τί οὖν τὸ σὸν οὐκ ἐπιτελεῖται, ἀλλὰ τὸ ἐξ ἡμῶν πλεονάζει, which is in the Greek. So are 'This is the reminder of comfort' (Αὕτη τῆς παραμυθίας ἡ ὑπόμνησις) and 'He says the earlier teachings correspond …' (Τὰ πρότερά φησι διδάγματα πρὸς τὰ ὕστερον συμβαίνοντα). The bracketed note on νῖκος/οἶκος transparently reports the printed text. The rest is idiom.
